scope: Only original fixed launcher and its five-test file; no builder review or compiler/network/proof execution.

findings.title: Retention expands bounded tmpfs contents into unbounded host disk usage
findings.observation: retain copies every regular-file path to the host mirror using copyfileobj without a shared retained-byte budget, sparse-file check or inode multiplicity policy. tmpfs limits allocated pages, not summed logical lengths. Sparse holes are materialized and hard links are duplicated.
findings.reproduction: Call quota_run(parent, mirror, inertPythonCommand,65536) in unshare --user --map-root-user --mount --fork. Child: create sparse with truncate(262144); create linked with 16384 bytes; os.link(linked,link0) through link7. Actual exit0;10 retained files;409600 logical bytes and409600 allocated host bytes. Temporary files removed afterwards.
findings.requiredChange: Enforce a cumulative retention byte ceiling before and during copying, reject unsupported sparse/hardlink representations or account their full copied cost, detect source mutation, and never let partial copies exceed the fixed host-retention allowance. Add actual namespace sparse/hardlink/growth regression controls.

findings.title: Child can write directly into the unbounded host mirror
findings.observation: The launcher bind-mounts the original host output directory at mirror before starting the command in that same mount namespace. The child retains writable access to mirror and other host paths allowed to the user. A private mount namespace and tmpfs at parent do not restrict these writes.
findings.reproduction: Call quota_run(parent, mirror, [python,-c,"import pathlib,sys; (pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])/"direct-host-output").write_bytes(b"x"*131072)",str(mirror)],65536) inside the same unshare configuration. Actual exit0 and131072 host bytes retained, with no tmpfs writes. Temporary files removed afterwards.
findings.requiredChange: For a hard child disk-confinement claim, prevent compiler descendants from writing the host retention mirror and other unbounded paths, using an enforced writable-path boundary or separate inaccessible retention context. A post-copy byte check alone does not close this direct-write path. If the intended claim is only a cooperative output-directory cap, explicitly narrow the claim and obtain the applicable resource decision before relying on it.
